body: Thanks Richard - Appreciate you finding these transcription issues. They are likely why the cipher was not solved. I'll check fix based off your feedback

Thanks again, Richard. All three are right. In this typewriter face the L has a serif only at the foot, and we had read it as I in SOLRS, ACCEL and FTULX. I re-read all 123 groups against the photograph at twice the size and found no other differences. The correction is in e0723da1b, and our 615 letters now give your SHA-256 (e266615d…), so we agree letter for letter. You're credited in the notes.

I also need to correct what I said above. Having re-run our tests on the corrected text, I don't think these letters are why it wasn't solved. They are substitutions, so no letter moves: the lag scan peaks at z = 3.4 (it was 3.3) at the same lags, and the index of coincidence is 0.0695 (was 0.0699). Our exclusions stand: every single transposition, the reversed-direction double columnar, and forward double columnar with a second key of ten letters or fewer. What's open is a double columnar with two long keys.

Your 160-letter hash doesn't match any stretch of this telegram, with or without BLUME SALAMANCA. Is it the second telegram? We only ever had the first (Klaus's post shows two, but only one is in its public preview), and our notes name the second as the best way in. If you can share it, or tell me where it comes from, I'd be very grateful, and you'd be credited, of course. And if you have a solution in progress, I'd be glad to link to it when you publish.

I can see the full second image without looking into FB e.g.

https://scontent.fsyd3-2.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t39.30808-6/495053957_23955786440685923_6316138309898944488_n.jpg?stp=dst-jpg_tt6&cstp=mx2048x1376&ctp=s2048x1376&_nc_cat=103&_nc_map=urlgen_bucketless&ccb=1-7&_nc_sid=127cfc&_nc_ohc=pcs9vuikF4sQ7kNvwFNwTy9&_nc_oc=AdpKbrcuEeHtuu2LMteB_9A222oduki1uk12xrmgcF9mWP26bMxAwwMkX8FOhKhxv10&_nc_zt=23&_nc_ht=scontent.fsyd3-2.fna&_nc_gid=mVYe1fEsG6dXfyUUiiE4LQ&_nc_ss=7b2a8&oh=00_AQNGRvBLtpwv4B-HhPZLkaJj0sMMr3Q7fm5pSTuYYcN7vQ&oe=6AC34D95

Does this help? The top comment on the post from William Higinbotham has a transcription, which matches the SHA-256 hash above.

Thank you, Richard, that's exactly what we were missing. I read the 32 groups from the full image, and they give your 8fd5cfb8… hash, so our transcription of the second telegram agrees with yours (and with William Higinbotham's, as you say). The photograph and transcription are now in the repo (9226922ff); the image link expires on 5 Oct, so the copy there matters. The form shows it went the same afternoon as the first: serial 1486, 14 fr, handed in at 17:34 (the first at 11:31).

160 letters against 615 isn't the equal-length depth the classical double-transposition attack needs. But if both telegrams used the same keys, any key pair has to make both read. I'm now testing on planted pairs whether that lets a joint search reach the long keys our single-message search couldn't, and I'll post what comes of it here.
